_comment: ONE source for the visual identity. Every profile gets
its own Monet palette; Home is deliberately colorless (glass) - color now
signals 'you are NOT home'.
launcher = which entry in .launchers gets the HOME role (40-theming.sh) and the
generated config (45-launcher-config.sh). Only Andashi Home is supported: the
release build (andashi-home) and its debug build (andashi-home-debug) for the
fork's e2e runs. Other launchers were dropped on purpose - each of them needed
UI automation that could type but never read back. Per entry: pkg, config,
wallpaper, glass, widgets.
wallpaper: true means the launcher applies appearance.wallpaper from its config
(Andashi Home 0.2.0+): gen-launcher.sh emits the key and 45-launcher-config.sh
uploads the image only then. Keep it false while an older release is pinned.
config: true means the launcher has a machine interface: provisioning pushes a
generated config/launcher/<profile>.json into the app's files dir and triggers
a reload + read-back verification (45-launcher-config.sh).
andashi-home is the fork (Andashi Home, org.andashi.home), the launcher this
distribution ships; andashi-home-debug is the same launcher as debug build for
the emulator tests (e2e/l4-*.sh in the fork use LAUNCHER_CONFIG_KEY=andashi-home-debug).
glass: true means the launcher renders the home screen as glass surfaces over the
blurred wallpaper (Andashi Home 0.5.0+, ADR 0004): gen-launcher.sh emits
appearance.glass and home.grid.labels and stops emitting appearance.transparency,
which 0.5.0 reports as an inert key. false keeps the old transparency block for an
older PINNED release - against 0.5.0 it fails the read-back, because the launcher
always serves a complete glass block back and never a transparency one.
The values live in all_profiles.glass and may be overridden per zone with a glass
object there; unlike the old transparency block those merge FIELD BY FIELD, so a
zone that wants another tint does not have to repeat blur, radius and contrast.
blur/radius are dp (0..64), tint is the alpha of the zone's Monet color over the
backdrop (0..1), contrast is low|medium|high and scales blur and tint together,
wallpaperBlur decides whether the WHOLE home background is the blurred copy.
It is false here, against the launcher default: the zone wallpapers are how a
zone announces itself, and blurred there is nothing left of any of them but a
colour field - a gradient would have done. The glass surfaces blur what is
behind them either way, so the look survives the sharp wallpaper.
All five fields are written explicitly because the launcher fills its defaults in on read-back
and the check compares the whole appearance section - an omitted field would read
as a difference.
palette = Monet seed (hex without #). SystemUI generates the color overlays from it
live (verified on emu64x: com.android.systemui:accent/neutral get [x]).
color_source=preset pins the color - changing the wallpaper does NOT change it.
style: TONAL_SPOT | VIBRANT | EXPRESSIVE | RAINBOW | FRUIT_SALAD | MONOCHROMATIC.
night: 2=dark 1=light 0=auto (secure/ui_night_mode). Takes effect immediately
for the active profile (cmd uimode), for background profiles only on the next profile switch.
icon_blacklist: hidden statusbar icons, comma-separated - keep the bar calm.
wallpaper: repo-relative path (themes/...), applied by Andashi Home itself for
home+lock screen: gen-launcher.sh puts appearance.wallpaper into the profile's
launcher.json, 45-launcher-config.sh uploads the image into the launcher's ingest
provider and reloads; the launcher reports the applied image in its read-back and
reapplies only when the file or the system wallpaper changed. Needs wallpaper: true
on the launcher entry (0.2.0+). 40-theming.sh restarts the launcher after a palette
change, because launchers cache icon tints until the process ends.
favorites (per profile): app LABELS, resolved by gen-launcher.sh against the catalog
(a label that does not resolve to exactly one entry fails generation) and written as
home.dock.favorites objects ({packageName: ...}) in the generated config.
WHAT THEY DO IN 0.3.0: the apps are pinned - they show up in the launcher's favorites
section in search and in the apps widget. They do NOT produce a dock band at the bottom:
that renderer hung in the clock widget and fell with it (andashi/home, 0.3.0). The key
home.dock.enabled is therefore inert for now and stays in the contract on purpose,
because the dock returns with the HomeGrid work (andashi/home ADR 0001) and removing
plus reintroducing it would be two contract changes instead of none.
Apps that aren't installed yet (e.g. Play apps on the emulator) simply are not pinned.
WARNING, unlike settings.json: per_profile WINS over all_profiles here.
All packages (launchers, keyboard_pkg) must be in the catalog
(10-apps.sh installs them), 40-theming.sh only activates (role, IME, wallpaper).
